Optimal.Notes: A 12 W TDP and 1400 MHz GPU clock give the GPU enough headroom to hold 30 fps more consistently than the battery profile, while FSR from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable on the 8-inch screen. This is the recommended starting point for most players.

profiles.Summary: Monster Hunter Wilds is a demanding modern 3D title that pushes well beyond the Steam Deck's hardware class — the minimum GPU spec (GTX 1660) is already above the Deck's RDNA 2 iGPU, so expect low settings, aggressive FSR upscaling, and a 30 fps target to keep things playable. The game is Steam Deck Verified and runs under Proton, but frame rates will be limited and battery life short without careful tuning.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB player reports were available; all three profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1660 minimum GPU, which exceeds the Deck's capability) and Deck hardware specifications. On first launch, check frame pacing in an open biome and during a monster encounter — if the Optimal profile dips below 25 fps, drop to Max Battery settings and reduce render resolution further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let FSR reconstruct to 1280x800 to relieve GPU pressure; a 9 W TDP cap extends battery but may cause occasional dips below 30 fps in dense environments. Install on the internal SSD for best streaming performance.

KnownIssues: Game targets hardware above the Steam Deck's GPU class; sustained 30 fps requires lowest settings and FSR upscaling.
No player-specific Deck reports found; settings are estimated from PC minimum requirements and Deck hardware analysis.
The game uses DirectStorage and REDengine-style streaming — loading from the internal SSD is strongly recommended over SD card.
Online/co-op sessions may increase CPU load and cause additional frame dips compared to solo play.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at full 15 W TDP with the GPU pinned to 1600 MHz squeezes out the most frames the Deck can realistically deliver; 40 fps is achievable in open-field areas but dense monster encounters or weather transitions may still dip to the low 30s. Expect significant heat and short battery life — best used plugged in or for short sessions.

Optimal.Notes: FSR Balanced at native 1280×800 output gives a sharper image than Performance mode while still targeting a stable 30 fps cap; raising TDP to 12 W keeps the GPU from throttling during busy multi-monster encounters. This is the recommended starting point — monitor GPU temperature and back off to MaxBattery settings if the device runs hot.
Optimal.ExpectedFps: 30 fps (mostly locked, dips to 25 in heavy fights)

profiles.Summary: Monster Hunter Wilds is a demanding 2025 AAA title that pushes well beyond the Steam Deck's GPU class, but CAPCOM's built-in upscaling (FSR/DLSS) and a "Lowest" preset targeting 720p→1080p/30 fps on minimum PC specs give the Deck a fighting chance at a playable 30 fps with heavy compromises. Expect frequent dips in dense environments and busy monster fights; keeping the frame cap at 30 and TDP at 15 W is essential for stability.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB reports with detailed settings were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1660 minimum, targeting 720p→1080p/30 fps on Lowest) versus the Deck's roughly GTX 1050 Ti-class GPU. On first run, check the frame rate counter in the opening outdoor area and during your first monster fight — if you cannot hold 25+ fps on Lowest with FSR Performance, the game may not be viable above 30 fps on this hardware.

MaxBattery.Notes: Prioritises battery by capping TDP to 8 W and leaning on FSR Performance mode; image quality will be noticeably soft but the game remains playable in camp and open-world traversal. Drop to 720p internal render in-game if frame rate dips below 25 fps in monster fights.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports yet — all profiles are hardware estimates based on PC minimum requirements and Deck GPU class.
The game's minimum GPU (GTX 1660 / RX 5500 XT) is significantly above the Deck's RDNA 2 8-CU GPU, so even Lowest settings may struggle in demanding areas.
Frame generation (used to hit 60 fps on recommended specs) is not supported on the Deck's RDNA 2 iGPU under Proton.
Shader compilation stutters are likely on first launch and first visit to new areas — run through content once to pre-compile shaders.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Targeting 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest motion the Deck can realistically sustain in this title; full 15 W TDP and max GPU clock are needed to approach the cap, and it will still drop in large-scale monster encounters. Do not raise settings above Lowest — the Deck's GPU simply cannot handle Medium or higher at any frame target.
MaxPerformance.ExpectedFps: 35-40 fps (drops to ~28 in the most demanding fights)
